newsitem.title: IRAN: Khatami says disputed isles belong to Iran, not UAE.
newsitem.headline: Khatami says disputed isles belong to Iran, not UAE.

text.p: Iranian president-elect Mohammad Khatami on Tuesday said three Gulf islands claimed by the United Arab Emirates belong to Iran, but urged bilateral negotiations to settle the dispute.
Khatami, a moderate former culture minister who won a landslide victory in last Friday's polls, told his first news conference "the islands belong to Iran".
But, speaking through an interpreter, he said the row over the islands "should be settled through friendly and open dialogue".
"It is actually a matter between two friendly and neighbourly countries...The intervention of other governments and powers would not be in the interest of either of us."

Since 1992 Iran and the UAE have been at loggerheads over Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunb islands that are close to key oil shipping lanes at the mouth of the Gulf. Gulf Arab states have long demanded an end to Iranian "occupation" of the islands.
Abu Dhabi has urged Tehran to agree to take the dispute to the International Court of Justice in The Hague. But Iran has said the row should be settled through negotiations.
The Tehran government has repeatedly said the islands are "inseparable parts of Iran". The UAE last year accused Iran of deploying offensive weapons on the islands.
